services.heading: What we do
services.intro: Four things, and they compound. Most projects start with the first one.

work.heading: Selected work
work.metricsNote: Outcomes and metrics are intentionally empty — those are real numbers, and they have to come from you.
work.pageHeading: Every one of these started from an empty file.
work.pageDescription: Websites built from an empty file for tour operators, camps and private villas.

call.title: A call
call.body: What the business needs, who it sells to, and what the current site fails to do. No deliverable is discussed yet — there is nothing to design until this part is clear.

scope.title: A written scope
scope.body: Pages, what each one has to accomplish, and the languages it ships in. Priced as a fixed quote, so the number does not move once work starts.

build.title: The build
build.body: Design and development against that scope, with a working link you can open at any point. Half up front, half on delivery.

handover.title: Handover
handover.body: Launch, plus the dashboard and a walkthrough of it. You edit your own content afterwards — text, prices, images, translations — without calling anyone.

testimonials.heading: From the people who paid for it

closing.heading: Tell us what the site has to do.
closing.body: A call, then a written scope with a fixed price. No obligation either way.

contact.title: Contact
contact.description: Tell us what the site has to do. A call, then a written scope with a fixed price.
contact.heading: Tell us what the site has to do.
contact.intro: The more you can say about the business — who buys from you, what they ask before booking, what the current site gets in the way of — the more useful the first reply will be.
contact.next1: A reply within a working day.
contact.next2: A short call — what the business needs, not what it should look like.
contact.next3: A written scope with a fixed price. No obligation.

about.title: About
about.description: Four things we will not do to your site, and four we will. Fixed scope, fixed price, no retainer, and the code is yours the day it ships.
about.heading: Four things we will not do. Four we will.
about.intro: No hedging, no small print. If any of this stops being true you will be the first to notice, which is rather the point of writing it down.

templates.note: Someone else's answer to someone else's problem, and every hour after installing it goes on bending it toward yours.

builders.note: Nested containers that mean nothing to a screen reader, a search engine, or the next developer who opens the file.

retainers.note: A site should not need a subscription to stay upright. If it does, something was built wrong.

surprises.note: A change halfway through is a conversation. You will never find out what it cost by reading a bill.

scope.note: Every page and every feature written down before anything is built — including what is explicitly not included.

price.note: Priced with the scope, and it does not move underneath you.

code.note: The repository is yours the day it ships. Another developer can pick it up without asking us for anything.

accounts.note: Domain, hosting and analytics in your name. Nothing is held hostage by being registered under ours.

about.deeperBody: Every step, what we need from you at each one, and roughly how long it takes.

approach.title: How we work
approach.description: The whole process, written down: every step of a JalimX project, what we need from you at each one, how long it takes, and what every site gets regardless of budget.
approach.body: Most studios will tell you it depends. Here is the sequence instead — what we need from you at each step, roughly how long each one takes, and what happens when you want to change something halfway through.

telemetry.label: This page, in your browser
telemetry.note: Read from your browser's Performance API as this page loaded. Not our numbers — yours. Reload and watch them settle.

approach.processIntro: Five steps. The only one with a variable length is the build, and the scope document tells you which end of the range you are at before you pay anything.
approach.processTerms: Half at scope, half at launch. Two review rounds included.

call.name: The call
call.body: A conversation, not a pitch. What the site has to do, who it is for, and what is not working now. If we are not the right people for it, you will hear that on this call rather than in week three.
call.need: Forty-five minutes, and honesty about the budget.

scope.name: The scope
scope.body: A written document: every page, every feature, what is explicitly not included, and one fixed price. You can hand it to another studio and get a comparable quote — that is rather the point of writing it down.
scope.need: Your content, or a decision that we write it.

build.name: The build
build.body: You get a link on the first day and it updates as we go. There is no reveal at the end. If something is wrong, it is wrong while it is still cheap to change.
build.need: Answers within a day or two, from one person.

review.name: Your review
review.body: You go through the whole thing and write one list. We work through the list. Two rounds are included in the price, and we have not yet needed a third.
review.need: One list, not five separate emails.

live.name: Live
live.body: Domain, certificate, redirects from whatever was there before, and a walkthrough of your dashboard — recorded, so you can watch it again in six months when you have forgotten.
live.need: Access to the domain, or we buy it in your name.

approach.standardIntro: Not a package tier. These are not negotiable down, because a site without them costs you more later than it saved you now.

standard.a: Fast on a phone on a bad connection — not just on a laptop on office wifi.
standard.b: Usable with a keyboard, and readable by a screen reader.
standard.c: Findable: real markup, real metadata, a real sitemap.
standard.d: Editable by you, from a dashboard built for your site rather than a generic admin panel.
standard.e: In both languages, if your customers are in both.
standard.f: Still standing in two years without a monthly retainer to keep it upright.

a.title: The content
a.body: Text, prices, images and translations, editable from a dashboard built for your site rather than a generic admin panel.

b.title: The code
b.body: The repository is yours. If we stop working together another developer picks it up — it is ordinary code in a framework you can hire for, not a proprietary system.

c.title: The domain and the accounts
c.body: Registered in your name, hosted under your account. Nothing is held hostage by being registered under ours.

approach.limitsIntro: Saying this out loud saves us both a call.

limits.a: Customise a WordPress or Shopify theme. If a theme is the right answer, you do not need us.
limits.b: Patch an existing page-builder site. Working inside one costs more than starting over, and the result is still built on the thing that caused the problem.
limits.c: Start without someone who can decide. We need one person on your side who can answer questions and sign things off. No amount of planning rescues a project that cannot get an answer.
